text: A gang robbed a mail train, then played Monopoly with the cash.
Let's go back to England, August nineteen sixty-three.
Now a Royal Mail train, the post office train, rolls through the night.
It's carrying sacks of used banknotes. Guess who wants them?
A gang of about fifteen men, with a plan.
Step one: they rig a signal, so the driver thinks he has to stop.
Hit like if you'd never have thought of that.
It stops at a bridge in the countryside.
Step two: they grab a hundred and twenty mail sacks.
Inside is about two point six million pounds.
That's around two and a half tons of cash, heavier than a car.
Step three: hide at a farmhouse.
And to pass the time? They play Monopoly with the real money.
Now send this to the friend who'd do the same.
But hiding means no trace, so they wipe the place down.
They planned to burn the farmhouse too. Reportedly, nobody did.
Then a tip sends police to the farm.
They wiped almost everything— well, almost.
But police found fingerprints on the Monopoly board, and on a ketchup bottle.
Wait, a board game and ketchup helped crack the case?
Follow if you love master plans beaten by board games.
In April nineteen sixty-four, a court convicted most of the gang.
The main men were sentenced to up to thirty years in prison.
Two and a half tons of cash, undone by a board game.
So, Monopoly or ketchup, which one was dumber?
